title: Global dimension formula for a surjective flat morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $d\in\mathbb N$. For $b\in Y$ write $X_b=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$ for its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Suppose $\dim_a(X_{f(a)})=d$ for every $a\in X$, where the point of the fibre corresponding to $a$ is understood and $\dim_a$ denotes the minimum of dimensions of open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Assume moreover that $f$ is surjective on underlying points and that $Y$ is nonempty. Then $$\dim X=\dim Y+d,$$ where both dimensions are the global topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $+\infty+d=+\infty$.

proof.text: For a point of either $X$ or $Y$, choose a member $U$ of the affine open covering with Noetherian section rings supplied by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The germ map from $\mathcal O(U)$ to its stalk is a localization by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], clause (c). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes every local ring of $X$ and $Y$ Noetherian. This checks the ring hypotheses needed below without assuming either scheme is quasi-compact or globally finite-dimensional.

source.place: Tag 0AFE (lemma-rel-dimension-dimension), second proof paragraph; expand the supremum argument using Properties 04MU (lemma-dimension) and Topology 0B7I (lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions)

proof.text: For $a\in X$, put $b=f(a)$, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,b}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,a}$, and $C=\mathcal O_{X_b,a}$, with the corresponding fibre point understood. By [def-weil-flat-morphism], $A\to B$ is flat and local, so the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $B$ is the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$ of $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to these maximal ideals. Localizing a local ring at its maximal ideal changes nothing: every denominator outside the maximal ideal is already a unit and $r/s\mapsto rs^{-1}$ is inverse to localization. Thus $\dim B=\dim A+\dim(B/\mathfrak m_AB)$. The isomorphism of [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] identifies the last ring with $C$. Ring isomorphisms preserve chains of prime ideals, so preserve dimension by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. We obtain, for every $a$, $$\dim\mathcal O_{X,a}=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,f(a)}+\dim\mathcal O_{X_{f(a)},a}.$$

source.place: Tag 0AFE (lemma-rel-dimension-dimension), second proof paragraph; expand the supremum argument using Properties 04MU (lemma-dimension) and Topology 0B7I (lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions)

proof.text: Fix $b\in Y$. Surjectivity and the homeomorphism onto $f^{-1}(b)$ in [def-pc-scheme-fibre] show that $X_b$ is nonempty, and every point $z$ of $X_b$ corresponds to a point $a$ over $b$. By hypothesis its local topological dimension is $d$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives $\dim X_b=\sup_{z\in X_b}d=d$. Applying [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] to $X_b$ now gives $$d=\sup_{z\in X_b}\dim\mathcal O_{X_b,z}.$$ Consequently every fibre stalk has dimension at most $d$, and at least one has dimension exactly $d$. Indeed, these dimensions are nonnegative integers since their supremum is the finite integer $d$ and a nonzero local ring has a maximal prime ideal. If $d=0$, any fibre point works. If $d>0$ and none attained $d$, all would be at most $d-1$, contradicting the displayed supremum. In particular, the fibre stalk dimension is not asserted to equal $d$ at every point.

source.place: Tag 0AFE (lemma-rel-dimension-dimension), second proof paragraph; expand the supremum argument using Properties 04MU (lemma-dimension) and Topology 0B7I (lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions)

proof.text: By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], $\dim X=\sup_{a\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,a}$ and $\dim Y=\sup_{b\in Y}\dim\mathcal O_{Y,b}$. Step 2 and the bound in Step 3 give, for every $a$, $$\dim\mathcal O_{X,a}\le\dim\mathcal O_{Y,f(a)}+d\le\dim Y+d.$$ Taking the supremum proves $\dim X\le\dim Y+d$. Conversely, for each $b$ choose a fibre point attaining $d$ as in Step 3 and let $a\in X$ be its image. Step 2 and the source supremum give $$\dim X\ge\dim\mathcal O_{Y,b}+d.$$ If $\dim Y=e<\infty$, the nonempty family of base-stalk dimensions has supremum the nonnegative integer $e$, so attains $e$: for $e>0$, failure would bound them by $e-1$, and for $e=0$ every base point works. Hence $\dim X\ge e+d$. If $\dim Y=\infty$, these stalk dimensions are unbounded or include infinity, and the same inequality gives $\dim X=\infty$. The base is nonempty by hypothesis, so no empty supremum occurs in this argument; surjectivity also makes $X$ nonempty. Both bounds give $\dim X=\dim Y+d$, including $d=0$ and infinite global dimension.
